problem.text: The sequence of numbers $t_1, t_2, t_3, \ldots$ is defined by $t_1 = 2$ and $$t_{n+1} = \frac{t_n - 1}{t_n + 1}$$ for every positive integer $n$. Determine the value of $t_{999}$.

steps.title: Where to start: work out the first few terms
steps.body: The question asks for term number $999$, far too many to compute one by one. When a rule like this asks for a very late term, the sequence often repeats. So compute the first few terms and watch for a value you have already seen.

steps.title: Keep going until a value comes back
The sequence repeats every $4$ terms
steps.body: Each term is computed only from the term before it. Since $t_5 = t_1$, the next terms copy the old ones: $t_6 = t_2$, $t_7 = t_3$, and so on. So the pattern $2, \frac{1}{3}, -\frac{1}{2}, -3$ repeats forever, and $t_n$ depends only on the remainder of $n$ when divided by $4$.

your_turn.answer: $n = 4, 8, 12, 16$: the multiples of $4$, because $t_4 = -3$ and the pattern has length $4$.

steps.title: Put it together
steps.body: Since $996 = 4\cdot 249$ is a multiple of $4$, $t_{996} = -3$. Going forward three terms: $t_{997} = 2$, $t_{998} = \frac{1}{3}$ and $t_{999} = -\frac{1}{2}$. The answer is **$-\frac{1}{2}$**.
